titre: The First Dinosaur Found With Down
accroche: In 1996, a Chinese farmer unearths a small dinosaur covered in filaments. Thirty years of skeletons reconstructed as gray and scaly waver with it.
contenu_vulgarise:
In August 1996, near the village of Sihetun, in China's Liaoning Province, a farmer uncovers a slab of limestone that splits into two nearly identical halves. Each preserves, in mirror image, the complete skeleton of a small carnivorous dinosaur 68 centimeters long, tail included. Around its back, its neck and along its tail, a fringe of fine filaments covers the rock. None of the tens of thousands of dinosaur fossils discovered until then had shown it so clearly. The animal receives a first name in 1996 in a Chinese journal, then a full description in English in the journal *Nature* in 1998, from the pens of paleontologists Chen Pei-ji, Dong Zhiming and Zhen Shuo-nan: *Sinosauropteryx prima*.

## Scales or Down?

The interpretation is not self-evident. The authors of 1998 remain cautious and speak of “protofeathers,” aware that the idea of a feathered dinosaur runs against a century of scientific imagery, that of the scaly, dull reptile, closer to the lizard than to the bird. A minority of researchers, including the ornithologist Alan Feduccia, propose another reading: these filaments would be decomposed collagen fibers, forming a simple dorsal crest, as in certain living aquatic lizards. The debate lasts nearly two decades, until a study in 2017 precisely compares the internal structure of the filaments with that of collagen and that of living feathers: the crest hypothesis does not hold. The structure does match primitive keratinous filaments, homologous to feathers.

## What the Discovery Finally Made Visible

The Liaoning deposit, the geological formation of Yixian, is dated to about 125 million years ago. Since 1996, it has yielded dozens of other dinosaurs with filaments or feathers, enough to establish that down is a widespread characteristic of small theropods, the very group from which birds descend. What followed went further than the mere presence of feathers. By analyzing under the electron microscope the melanosomes, those cellular structures responsible for pigmentation, a British team reconstructed in 2017 the real color pattern of *Sinosauropteryx*: a light belly and a dark back, a classic camouflage of an animal of open terrain, the opposite of the image of the monochrome reptile that had dominated museums throughout the 20th century. An animal gone for 125 million years has thus given back, skin fossil after skin fossil, information that was thought lost along with color itself: the palette of a living dinosaur.

repere.texte: The Yixian Formation, where Sinosauropteryx was found in 1996, is dated to about 125 million years ago. It took 21 years and an analysis of the internal structure of the filaments to rule out, in 2017, the hypothesis of a simple collagen crest in favor of primitive feathers.
repere.source: Chen, Dong & Zhen, Nature, 1998; Smithwick, Mayr, Saitta, Benton & Vinther, Palaeontology, 2017

carte.punch: Filamented dinosaur unearthed in 1996: it takes until 2017 to rule out the collagen hypothesis.
carte.idee: In 1996, a Chinese fossil reveals a small dinosaur fringed with filaments. Some see mere collagen fibers; a 2017 study rules out this hypothesis in favor of primitive feathers, and another reconstructs its color: light belly, dark back, a camouflage of open terrain.

pour_aller_plus_loin.note: Account of the 1996 discovery at Sihetun and of the rise of the feathered fossils of Liaoning.

quiz.question: Why did it take paleontologists nearly twenty years to confirm that Sinosauropteryx wore true primitive feathers?
choix: Because the original fossil was lost shortly after its discovery
Because the filaments also resembled decomposed collagen fibers, another plausible explanation
Because no laboratory could date the rock precisely
Because Chinese and Western researchers refused to share their data
quiz.explication: Some researchers, including Alan Feduccia, proposed that the filaments were collagen fibers forming a dorsal crest rather than feathers. It took a detailed analysis of their internal structure, in 2017, to decide between the two hypotheses in favor of feathers. The fossil itself was never lost: it is still being studied today.

quiz_supplementaire.question: How was the Sinosauropteryx fossil uncovered in 1996?
choix: By a team of Chinese paleontologists on an organized expedition
By a farmer, near the village of Sihetun, in Liaoning
By workers digging a railway tunnel
By divers exploring a dried-up lake
quiz_supplementaire.explication: It is a farmer who uncovers the limestone slab near the village of Sihetun, in China's Liaoning Province, in August 1996.

quiz_supplementaire.question: What did the analysis of Sinosauropteryx's fossilized melanosomes, published in 2017, reveal?
choix: A uniformly gray coat, close to that of living lizards
Brightly colored feathers, red and blue, like some tropical birds
A light belly and a dark back, a camouflage of open terrain
A coloration impossible to determine for lack of preservation
quiz_supplementaire.explication: The British team reconstructs in 2017 a precise color pattern: light belly and dark back, a classic camouflage of an animal of open terrain.

quiz_supplementaire.question: What have the dozens of other fossils found at the Liaoning deposit since 1996 established?
choix: That down is a widespread characteristic of small theropods
That Sinosauropteryx remained the only known dinosaur to bear filaments
That all the dinosaurs of Liaoning belonged to the same species
quiz_supplementaire.explication: The dozens of fossils found since 1996 at the Liaoning deposit show that down is widespread in small theropods, from which birds descend.
